sentences.text:
Applicant :- Kamil
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Mukhtar Alam Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,V.P. Singh Kashyap Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. None appeared on behalf of the informant even in revised call, however, learned AGA for the State is present.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Mukhtar Alam, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Santish Nigam, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
4.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
585 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) IPC & 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station- Sector 39,
District- Gautambuddha Nagar, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

5. FIR of the present case was lodged against unknown person and according to the FIR,
sister-in-law of the informant aged about 14 years on 14.09.2022 had gone from her house but she did not return.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant was not named in the FIR but when the victim was recovered and her statement was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. then she stated that she had gone along with the applicant and thereafter applicant was made accused in the present matter.

7. He further submitted that from the perusal of the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. it is apparent that she had gone along with the applicant according to her own wish and she appears to be consenting party.

He further submitted that on previous date this Court directed the CMO concerned to conduct the ossification test of the victim and now the ossification test of the victim has been conducted and report of the same is on record and as per the ossification test report, at the time of incident she was around 15-16 years' old.

8. He further submitted that although, victim appears to be below 18 years of age at the time of incident but applicant is also a young boy and it is a case of love affair and he is not having any criminal history and is in jail since 24.09.2022 i.e. for almost a year.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that as per the ossification test report of the victim, which was conducted after the direction of this Court, at the time of incident she was around 15-16 years' old and therefore, her consent is immaterial but could not dispute the fact that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 24.09.2023 and from the statements of the prosecutrix recorded during investigation, it appears that she had gone along with the applicant according to her own wish.
10.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. From the record, it reflects that victim was an illiterate lady and during investigation her ossification test was not conducted, therefore, on previous date this Court directed the CMO concerned to conduct the ossification test of the victim and pursuant to the order passed by this Court, ossification test of the victim was conducted and the same was forwarded to this Court.

From the perusal of the ossification test report of the victim, it appears that in the month of May, 2023 she was around 16 years' old, therefore, it appears that victim may be around 15-16 years' old at the time of incident but there is margin of two years from either side of the age mentioned in the ossification test report of the victim, therefore, from this angle victim might be even 17 years' old at the time of incident.

12. Further, victim in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C.
categorically stated that she had gone along with the applicant according to her own wish and she appears to be consenting party.
13. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 24.09.2022 i.e. for almost a year.
14. Law is settled that bail application should not be dismissed either for preventive or for punitive purposes.

sentences.text: Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
16. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

17. Let the applicant- Kamil be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
18. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

19. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
